provenance: Editorial TOPIK II Level 4 grammar selection, not an official TOPIK level checklist; educator review required.

grammarPoints.title: -잖아요
grammarPoints.hint: Remind someone of something you expect they already know, often to justify a point.
grammarPoints.description: Remind someone of something you expect they already know, often to justify a point.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 잖아요 to a verb or descriptive stem: 알다 → 알잖아요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 오늘 바쁘잖아요. — You know we're busy today. 바쁘잖아요 appeals to shared knowledge that the listener is busy.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Tone matters: it can sound reproachful if you insist the listener should know.

lessonExamples.englishHint: You know we're busy today.
You know that movie is good.

cards.englishHint: You know there's no time.
I told you yesterday, remember?
You know this road is faster.

grammarPoints.title: -거든요
grammarPoints.hint: Supply background information or a reason that the listener may not know.
grammarPoints.description: Supply background information or a reason that the listener may not know.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 거든요 to the predicate stem: 바쁘다 → 바쁘거든요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 먼저 갈게요. 약속이 있거든요. — I'll leave first. I have an appointment. 약속이 있거든요 provides the reason for leaving early.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: The reason-giving ending is usually sentence-final; -거든 as a condition is a separate use.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I'll leave first. I have an appointment.
I'll rest today because I'm tired.

cards.englishHint: I come often because I live nearby.
I can't right now; I have lots of work.

cards.fullSentence: 그 음식은 못 먹어요. 알레르기가 있거든요.
cards.englishHint: I can't eat that; I have an allergy.

grammarPoints.title: -더니
grammarPoints.hint: Connect a past observation with a later change or result.
grammarPoints.description: Connect a past observation with a later change or result.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 더니 to the stem of what was observed, then state what happened next.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 비가 오더니 곧 그쳤어요. — It rained, then stopped soon afterward. 비가 오더니 shows the observed rain before the weather cleared.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Do not simply use -더니 to report your own past deliberate action; it has an observation perspective.

lessonExamples.englishHint: It rained, then stopped soon afterward.
The child cried and then fell asleep.

cards.englishHint: It was cold, then became warm.
My friend laughed and suddenly cried.
The sky clouded over and then it rained.

grammarPoints.title: -았/었더니
grammarPoints.hint: After the speaker performed an action, a result or discovery followed.
grammarPoints.description: After the speaker performed an action, a result or discovery followed.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Put a past form before 더니: 먹다 → 먹었더니.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 약을 먹었더니 나아졌어요. — I took medicine and felt better. 약을 먹었더니 demonstrates an action followed by an improvement.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Unlike observational -더니, -았/었더니 often follows something the speaker personally did.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I took medicine and felt better.
I opened the door and found a cat.

cards.englishHint: I slept early and am not tired.
I went and found many people.
I walked a lot and now my legs hurt.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다
grammarPoints.hint: Pretend that something is true or that you are doing an action.
grammarPoints.description: Pretend that something is true or that you are doing an action.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 척하다 for actions, or -(으)ㄴ 척하다 for a present state.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 아이는 자는 척했어요. — The child pretended to be asleep. 자는 척했어요 describes pretending to sleep, not actually sleeping.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This can imply deception or playful pretense; it is not a normal statement of appearance.

lessonExamples.englishHint: The child pretended to be asleep.
He pretended not to know.

cards.englishHint: I pretended to be okay.
My friend pretended not to hear.
He pretended to be busy.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다
grammarPoints.hint: Assert that something cannot possibly be true, based on reasoning.
grammarPoints.description: Assert that something cannot possibly be true, based on reasoning.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -(으)ㄹ before the separate noun 리, followed by 가 없어요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 그분이 거짓말할 리가 없어요. — There is no way that person would lie. 그분이 거짓말할 리가 없어요 expresses strong disbelief that they would lie.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is a strong judgment, not merely the uncertain possibility in -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다.

lessonExamples.englishHint: There is no way that person would lie.
It can't possibly be this easy.

cards.englishHint: He can't have forgotten the appointment.
They can't all have been wrong.
That story can't possibly be true.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다
grammarPoints.hint: Express that there is no other choice or possible outcome.
grammarPoints.description: Express that there is no other choice or possible outcome.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Add -(으)ㄹ to the stem, then 수밖에 없어요 as separate words.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 지금은 기다릴 수밖에 없어요. — For now we have no choice but to wait. 기다릴 수밖에 없어요 means waiting is the only option left.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Do not confuse with -(으)ㄹ 수 없다, which says the action is impossible.

lessonExamples.englishHint: For now we have no choice but to wait.
Without money, I have no choice but to walk.

cards.englishHint: Because of the rain, we have to cancel.

cards.fullSentence: 시간이 없어 택시를 탈 수밖에 없어요.
cards.englishHint: We're forced to take a taxi because of time.

cards.fullSentence: 자료가 부족해서 다시 조사할 수밖에 없어요.
cards.englishHint: We must investigate again for lack of data.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ 채로
grammarPoints.hint: Leave one state unchanged while another action takes place.
grammarPoints.description: Leave one state unchanged while another action takes place.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -(으)ㄴ after the state or resulting action, then 채로.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 신발을 신은 채로 들어왔어요. — Someone came in with their shoes on. 신발을 신은 채로 means that the shoes remain on during the next action.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Unlike -고, 채로 emphasizes maintaining a state instead of a simple sequence.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Someone came in with their shoes on.
I went out leaving the door open.

cards.englishHint: I fell asleep with the lights on.
I swam with my glasses on.
I thought with my eyes closed.

lessons.title: Worth trying, wasted effort and blame

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ 만하다
grammarPoints.hint: Judge an action as worthwhile or a result as reasonably good.
grammarPoints.description: Judge an action as worthwhile or a result as reasonably good.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)ㄹ 만하다 to an action verb, conjugating 만하다 as 만해요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 이 책은 읽을 만해요. — This book is worth reading. 읽을 만해요 means the book is worth reading, not necessarily outstanding.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Do not confuse with -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, which measures ability rather than worth.

lessonExamples.englishHint: This book is worth reading.
That movie is worth watching.

cards.englishHint: This restaurant is worth visiting.
This problem is manageable.
That place is worth recommending.

grammarPoints.title: -아/어 봤자
grammarPoints.hint: An attempted action is pointless because it cannot change the outcome.
grammarPoints.description: An attempted action is pointless because it cannot change the outcome.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Make the verb's 아/어 form, followed by 봤자; the result is often negative.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 지금 가 봤자 늦어요. — Even if you go now, it's too late. 지금 가 봤자 늦어요 means going now won't help: it's already too late.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is not ordinary -아/어 보다 ('try doing'); -아/어 봤자 dismisses the usefulness.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Even if you go now, it's too late.
Asking won't get you an answer.

cards.englishHint: Regretting it won't help.
Hurrying won't help; we're late already.

cards.fullSentence: 혼자 고민해 봤자 해결이 안 돼요.
cards.englishHint: Worrying alone won't solve it.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에
grammarPoints.hint: Blame an action or condition for an unwelcome result.
grammarPoints.description: Blame an action or condition for an unwelcome result.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 after an ongoing action or -(으)ㄴ after a completed action before 탓에.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 잠을 못 잔 탓에 피곤해요. — I'm tired because I didn't sleep enough. 잠을 못 잔 탓에 says lack of sleep caused a negative condition.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: 덕분에 credits helpful causes; 탓에 usually assigns blame or an unfortunate cause.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I'm tired because I didn't sleep enough.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 비가 많이 온 탓에 길이 막혔어요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: The roads jammed because of heavy rain.

cards.englishHint: We failed due to insufficient preparation.
We were late because we left late.
I made a mistake because I rushed.

grammarPoints.title: -는 김에
grammarPoints.hint: Do something extra while already taking an opportunity to do something else.
grammarPoints.description: Do something extra while already taking an opportunity to do something else.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 김에 after an action being undertaken, then add a second useful action.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 장 보는 김에 우유도 사 주세요. — Since you're shopping, buy milk too. 장 보는 김에 asks the listener to buy milk while already shopping.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is opportunistic convenience, not simply two consecutive actions with -고.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 장 보는 김에 우유도 사 주세요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Since you're shopping, buy milk too.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 은행에 가는 김에 돈을 찾아 주세요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Since you're going to the bank, withdraw cash.

cards.englishHint: I took out trash while going outside.
Since I came to Seoul, I met a friend.
While cleaning, I wiped the windows too.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ까 봐
grammarPoints.hint: A feared possibility becomes the reason for caution or precaution.
grammarPoints.description: A feared possibility becomes the reason for caution or precaution.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Add -(으)ㄹ까 봐 to the feared event, then describe the precaution.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 늦을까 봐 일찍 나왔어요. — I left early for fear of being late. 늦을까 봐 says fear of being late motivated an early departure.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is not an ordinary question -ㄹ까요?; it expresses anxiety about an outcome.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I left early for fear of being late.
I packed an umbrella in case it rains.

cards.englishHint: I checked again in case I'd made a mistake.
I checked a map for fear of getting lost.
I'm worried I might fail the exam.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다
grammarPoints.hint: Sum up a situation as effectively amounting to something: 'basically / in effect'.
grammarPoints.description: Sum up a situation as effectively amounting to something: 'basically / in effect'.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 셈이다 for actions and -(으)ㄴ 셈이다 for completed actions or states.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 이 정도면 성공한 셈이에요. — At this point it's effectively a success. 이 정도면 성공한 셈이에요 judges the outcome as effectively a success.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is an interpretation of the facts, not a literal identity statement with 이에요.

lessonExamples.englishHint: At this point it's effectively a success.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 하루에 두 번이면 자주 가는 셈이에요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Twice a day counts as going often.

cards.fullSentence: 돈을 다 썼으니 남은 게 없는 셈이에요.
cards.englishHint: Having spent it all, there's effectively none left.
Practicing daily effectively makes it consistent.
In effect, we started over.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 데다가
grammarPoints.hint: Add another factor on top of the first one, often intensifying the result.
grammarPoints.description: Add another factor on top of the first one, often intensifying the result.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 데다가 for action verbs, -(으)ㄴ 데다가 for descriptive verbs.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 비가 오는 데다가 바람도 불어요. — It's raining, and it's windy on top of that. 비가 오는 데다가 adds wind as another factor making the weather unpleasant.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Don't confuse with location noun 데. Both factors generally point in the same direction.

lessonExamples.englishHint: It's raining, and it's windy on top of that.
It's expensive and the quality is bad too.

cards.englishHint: He's kind and also good at his job.
It's quiet here and transport is convenient.
The trip is long and traffic is bad too.

grammarPoints.title: -았/었어야 하다
grammarPoints.hint: Express regret or criticism that an action should have happened in the past.
grammarPoints.description: Express regret or criticism that an action should have happened in the past.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Take the past -았/었 form and add 어야 했어요: 가다 → 갔어야 했어요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 더 일찍 출발했어야 했어요. — We should have left earlier. 일찍 출발했어야 했어요 admits the needed departure happened too late.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This differs from present -아/어야 해요, which talks about what must be done now or next.

lessonExamples.englishHint: We should have left earlier.
I should have said something then.

cards.englishHint: I should have studied a bit more.
I should have brought an umbrella.
We should have booked first.

grammarPoints.title: -았/었더라면
grammarPoints.hint: Imagine an unreal past condition and a result that did not actually happen.
grammarPoints.description: Imagine an unreal past condition and a result that did not actually happen.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Build the past verb form and add 더라면, then say what would have followed.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 조금 일찍 왔더라면 만났을 거예요. — If I'd come earlier, I would have met them. 조금 일찍 왔더라면 says arriving earlier did not happen, so the result is hypothetical.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: It signals a counterfactual past, not a realistic future condition like -(으)면.

lessonExamples.englishHint: If I'd come earlier, I would have met them.
If I'd known earlier, I'd have prepared.

cards.englishHint: If I'd had money, I'd have bought it.
Had I studied then, I'd have passed.
If it hadn't rained, I would have gone.

grammarPoints.title: -더라도
grammarPoints.hint: Concede an unfavorable or extreme condition without changing the decision.
grammarPoints.description: Concede an unfavorable or extreme condition without changing the decision.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 더라도 to the stem and state what remains true even in that case.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 힘들더라도 끝내세요. — Even if it's hard, finish it. 힘들더라도 끝내세요 means to finish even if doing so is difficult.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Unlike a simple -아/어도, -더라도 can present a firmer hypothetical concession.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Even if it's hard, finish it.
We'll depart even if it rains.

cards.englishHint: Even if you're busy, eat a meal.
Even if I fail, I'll try again.
Even if it's expensive, it's needed.

grammarPoints.title: -는 한
grammarPoints.hint: Specify the condition under which something continues to hold: 'as long as'.
grammarPoints.description: Specify the condition under which something continues to hold: 'as long as'.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 는 한 to an action stem; the following clause is valid while that condition holds.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 노력하는 한 기회는 있어요. — As long as you try, there's a chance. 노력하는 한 means success is possible for as long as effort continues.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Don't use this for a single cause in the past; it sets an ongoing condition.

lessonExamples.englishHint: As long as you try, there's a chance.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 비가 오는 한 밖에 못 나가요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: As long as it rains, we can't go out.

cards.englishHint: As far as I know, it's true.

cards.fullSentence: 여기서 사는 한 규칙을 지켜야 해요.
cards.englishHint: As long as you live here, follow the rules.
As long as you practice, you'll improve.

grammarPoints.title: -느니
grammarPoints.hint: Prefer one option over another, often with 'rather than doing X'.
grammarPoints.description: Prefer one option over another, often with 'rather than doing X'.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Add 느니 to an action stem, followed by the option that seems better.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 기다리느니 걸어갈래요. — I'd rather walk than wait. 기다리느니 걸어갈래요 prefers walking to waiting.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This evaluates alternatives; -거나 merely lists alternatives without stating a preference.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I'd rather walk than wait.
I'd rather try again than give up.

cards.englishHint: Tell the truth rather than lie.
Ask for help rather than do it alone.
I'd rather go tomorrow than go late.

grammarPoints.title: -자고 하다
grammarPoints.hint: Report another person's suggestion to do something together: 'said let's'.
grammarPoints.description: Report another person's suggestion to do something together: 'said let's'.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Take a verb stem and add 자고 하다, conjugating 하다 in the reporting tense.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 친구가 같이 가자고 했어요. — My friend suggested we go together. 같이 가자고 했어요 reports a proposal without repeating it as direct speech.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: -자고 is for proposals; -라고 is used for commands and -냐고 for questions.

lessonExamples.englishHint: My friend suggested we go together.
My sibling suggested watching a movie.

cards.englishHint: A senior suggested meeting early.
A friend proposed having lunch.
A teammate suggested discussing it again.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)라고 하다
grammarPoints.hint: Report an instruction or command that another person gave.
grammarPoints.description: Report an instruction or command that another person gave.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 으라고 after most consonant verb stems and 라고 after vowel stems, then 하다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 선생님이 일찍 오라고 했어요. — The teacher told us to come early. 오라고 했어요 quotes a request to come early without using direct quotation marks.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: A quoted command differs from the quoted suggestion -자고 하다.

lessonExamples.englishHint: The teacher told us to come early.
Mom told me to eat.

cards.englishHint: The doctor told me to rest.
My friend told me to close the door.
My boss told me to check again.

grammarPoints.title: -냐고 하다
grammarPoints.hint: Report what someone ASKED, keeping the reported sentence as a question.
grammarPoints.description: Report what someone ASKED, keeping the reported sentence as a question.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 냐고 to the reported question predicate; use 묻다 or 하다 for the report.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 친구가 언제 오냐고 물었어요. — My friend asked when I was coming. 언제 오냐고 물었어요 reports the question 'When are you coming?'.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Don't use declarative -다고 to report a question, or imperative -라고 for a question.

lessonExamples.englishHint: My friend asked when I was coming.
That person asked where I live.

cards.englishHint: The child asked why I was laughing.
The teacher asked if I was ready.
My friend asked what I was eating.

grammarPoints.title: -대요 (contracted report)
grammarPoints.hint: Give hearsay using the shortened form of -다고 해요: 'they say that...'.
grammarPoints.description: Give hearsay using the shortened form of -다고 해요: 'they say that...'.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: With present actions, -ㄴ/는대요 can replace -ㄴ/는다고 해요; descriptions use -대요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 내일 비가 온대요. — They say it'll rain tomorrow. 내일 비가 온대요 means someone reported that rain is expected tomorrow.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Don't confuse -대요 (reported information) with -데요 (speaker's reaction/experience).

lessonExamples.englishHint: They say it'll rain tomorrow.
They say the restaurant is good.

cards.englishHint: They say my friend is studying now.
Apparently it finishes early today.
They say that movie is entertaining.
